title: Cap. III Rat. 6: mercy with justice needs elect congruitas; Javellus
pass_a_gloss: Reason 6. In all the works of God mercy concurs with justice: Therefore we ought to posit on the part of the elect some fittingness or congruity which was not on the part of the reprobate; otherwise no vestige of justice will appear in this election of God: And that he elects from foresight, and not from the mere good pleasure of his will. It is the argument of Javellus in the Questions annexed to the first part of Aquinas.
pass_b_english: Rat. 6. In all God's works mercy concurs with justice — so, they say, we must posit on the elect's side some fittingness or congruity that was not on the reprobate's; otherwise no trace of justice will show in this election of God — and that he elects from foresight, not from the mere good pleasure of his will. So argues Javellus in the Questions annexed to Aquinas's Prima Pars.
source_text: Rat. 6. In omnibus operibus Dei misericordia concurrit cum justitia: Ergo ponere debemus ex parte electi aliquam convenientiam sive congruitatem, quae non fuit ex parte reprobi; secus nullum justitiae vestigium in hac Dei electione apparebit: Et quod elegit ex praevisione, et non ex mero beneplacito voluntatis suae. Est argumentum Javelli in Quaestionibus adjunctis primae parti Aquinatis.
